page.overview:
Who is Man in the Moon?

The Man in the Moon was a character that exists within the folk-tales of the Shire-folk,

The Man in the Moon of the Hobbits' tales may have his origins in the legend of Tilion the Maia.

The Númenóreans believed that the Man in the Moon, like the Lady of the Sun, was a guardian spirit.

According to Middle-earth folklore, the Man in the Moon had silver shoes and a silver beard as well as a pale gray mantle. His girdlestead was said to be crowned with opals and pearls. He lived in a white minaret towering over the Mountains of the Moon that was made out of diamonds and "tall moonstone" and had "an ivory door" that was only unlockable with a "crystal key" that he possessed.
